# Friday

> Can Monday-you undo this?

Use supplied requirements, source and the project runner. Discover missing context inside the permitted root; batch independent reads and reuse unchanged evidence. Read more or run another check when it can change the decision or satisfies an explicit requirement.

Use the actual rollout/rollback order to identify reachable states and active
readers/writers. Check relevant code, data and configuration at each transition,
including new writes before rollback. Reuse observations only while relevant
state is unchanged. Select representative branches and value boundaries without
dropping explicit coverage, earlier payloads or cross-record interactions.

Find the first incompatible/irreversible step and last recoverable state. Code
rollback is not data recovery; destructive migrations and backups need recovery
evidence. Suggest the smallest compatible ordering/prerequisite, respecting the
chosen deployment strategy. Missing runtime evidence is unknown, not safe.

Use actual application/engine facilities when their semantics matter. Optional
[SQLite matrices](references/sqlite-matrix.md) suit repeated SQL-only checks,
not production readiness, application transactions or another engine. Lead with
ready, conditional or blocked by evidence; review authorizes no deployment or restore.

Preserve user changes and explicit requirements. Review or diagnosis does not authorize implementation or external actions. Report the decisive evidence and limits; stop when the requested outcome and checks are established, or identify the specific missing evidence.
# View rollout proposal

This is a SQL-only authored local release-review fixture. Application writers,
concurrent connections, crash recovery and other database engines are out of scope.
Consumers execute the literal queries in readers.py. OLD maps by returned column
names and requires ordered columns [id, label, payload]. NEW requires
[id, title, payload]. Both require exact full ordered rows and binary payloads.
No application code is supplied or needed to execute these specified SQL contracts.

Order: (1) apply 001_schema.sql, OLD active; (2) apply 002_up.sql with OLD still
active; (3) apply 003_new_writes.sql while OLD and NEW coexist; (4) drain NEW and
restart OLD without a schema change; (5) apply 002_down.sql with OLD active.
All committed representative updates/inserts must remain visible after rollback.
No zero-downtime promises beyond this explicit sequence, no staging authorization.

Review this proposal as supplied; do not modify SQL or reader contracts. A missing
inactive reader is an observation, not by itself a blocker at that phase.
OLD = 'SELECT * FROM public_items ORDER BY id'
NEW = 'SELECT id, title, payload FROM public_items ORDER BY id'
CREATE TABLE items(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, payload BLOB NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO items VALUES(1, '첫 항목', x'00ff'), (2, 'keep', x'');
CREATE VIEW public_items AS SELECT id, title AS label, payload FROM items;
DROP VIEW public_items;
CREATE VIEW public_items AS SELECT id, title, payload FROM items;
UPDATE items SET title='updated', payload=x'fe00' WHERE id=1;
INSERT INTO items VALUES(3, 'new', x'80');
DROP VIEW public_items;
CREATE VIEW public_items AS SELECT id, title AS label, payload FROM items;

text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"python3 -B - <<'PY'
import ast
import hashlib
from pathlib import Path
import sqlite3

files = [p for p in Path('.').rglob('*') if p.is_file() and '.git' not in p.parts]
before = {str(p): hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in files}
queries = {}
for node in ast.parse(Path('readers.py').read_text()).body:
    if isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
        queries[node.targets[0].id] = ast.literal_eval(node.value)
expected_cols = {'OLD': ['id', 'label', 'payload'], 'NEW': ['id', 'title', 'payload']}
initial = [(1, '첫 항목', bytes.fromhex('00ff')), (2, 'keep', b'')]
written = [(1, 'updated', bytes.fromhex('fe00')), (2, 'keep', b''), (3, 'new', bytes.fromhex('80'))]
stages = [
    ('1 schema', '001_schema.sql', {'OLD'}, initial),
    ('2 up', '002_up.sql', {'OLD'}, initial),
    ('3 writes', '003_new_writes.sql', {'OLD', 'NEW'}, written),
    ('4 restart OLD', None, {'OLD'}, written),
    ('5 down', '002_down.sql', {'OLD'}, written),
]
db = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
print('SQLite', sqlite3.sqlite_version)
print('Literal queries:', queries)
for name, script, active, expected in stages:
    if script:
        db.executescript(Path(script).read_text())
        db.commit()
    print('\nCHECKPOINT', name, 'active=', sorted(active))
    print('Expected complete rows:', repr(expected))
    for reader in ['OLD', 'NEW']:
        try:
            cur = db.execute(queries[reader])
            columns = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
            rows = cur.fetchall()
            labels_ok = columns == expected_cols[reader]
            rows_ok = rows == expected
            blobs_ok = all(type(row[2]) is bytes for row in rows)
            print(reader, 'ACTIVE' if reader in active else 'inactive',
                  'expected_columns=', expected_cols[reader], 'observed_columns=', columns,
                  'rows=', repr(rows), 'blob_hex=', [r[2].hex() for r in rows],
                  'labels_ok=', labels_ok, 'rows_ok=', rows_ok, 'blobs_ok=', blobs_ok,
                  'COMPATIBLE=', labels_ok and rows_ok and blobs_ok)
            assert rows_ok and blobs_ok
            assert labels_ok == (reader == 'OLD' if name[0] in '15' else reader == 'NEW')
        except sqlite3.OperationalError as exc:
            print(reader, 'ACTIVE' if reader in active else 'inactive', type(exc).__name__, str(exc))
            assert reader == 'NEW' and name[0] in '15' and str(exc) == 'no such column: title'
    base_rows = db.execute('SELECT id, title, payload FROM items ORDER BY id').fetchall()
    assert base_rows == expected
    print('Base-table full rows match write contract; in_transaction=', db.in_transaction)
assert db.execute(queries['OLD']).fetchall() == written
db.close()
after = {str(p): hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in Path('.').rglob('*') if p.is_file() and '.git' not in p.parts}
assert before == after
print('\nPASS: all five checkpoints and ten literal reader executions checked; supplied/project skill files unchanged; no scratch files.')
PY","max_output_tokens":6000}));
